title: Interior Design Ideas for DLF Aralias Apartments: Balancing Heritage Layouts with Modern Luxury
author: Shivam Kumar

featuredImage.alt: Luxury living room interior by The Omega Group, with a textured feature wall and warm wood tones

excerpt: DLF Aralias apartments have excellent bones: generous rooms and golf course views. What's aged is the kitchens, bathrooms, wiring and lighting. See what to keep, refresh or replace, and the right order to renovate.
keyTakeaways: The Layout Is an Asset — Aralias homes have generous, well-separated rooms; most renovations should update the plan, not reinvent it.
The Hidden Systems Are the Real Age — Wiring, plumbing, air-conditioning and waterproofing from the 2000s are usually the real renovation priority, even when surfaces look fine.
Restore Marble Before Replacing It — Original stone can often be ground, repaired and polished; full replacement across 5,600+ sq ft is costly and disruptive.
Rebuild Bathrooms from the Waterproofing Up — After 15+ years, bathrooms are the most likely place to hide leaks, and a leak affects the apartment below.
Society Approval Comes Before Demolition — Structural wall changes need a structural engineer's sign-off and the estate office's approval, plus agreed work hours and deposits.
Budget ₹2,500–₹8,000+ per Sq Ft and 4–6 Months — The 2026 luxury planning range; renovations with structural or waterproofing work can run longer.
contentHtml:
The best Aralias renovations keep the generous original room proportions and golf-course orientation, and update everything that has aged: services, kitchens, bathrooms, lighting and automation. Plan the hidden work first (wiring, plumbing, air-conditioning, waterproofing), confirm any wall change with a structural engineer and the society, and expect a full renovation of a 4BHK to take several months.

DLF The Aralias was one of Gurgaon's first true luxury condominiums, and many of its homes are now well over a decade old. The bones are excellent: large rooms, golf course views and a calm, low-density setting. What has aged are the parts that change fastest: kitchens, bathrooms, lighting, wiring and controls. This guide covers DLF Aralias interior design for owners and new buyers who want a modern home without losing what made the original plan good.

DLF Aralias at a glance

DetailWhat is on record
LocationSector 42, Golf Course Road, within DLF5 Golf Links
Homes254 residences in 11 towers (DLF)
LandAbout 12.5 acres (DLF)
Configurations4BHK apartments of roughly 5,600 to 6,000 sq ft, plus penthouses of about 10,000 sq ft and above (listings)
AgeDelivered in the late 2000s, according to listings
Asking prices, 2026About ₹35 crore and up for a 4BHK; roughly ₹58,500 to ₹65,000 per sq ft (listings)
SettingGolf course views, low density, signature clubhouse

Why Aralias homes need a different brief

A new luxury apartment is designed from scratch. An Aralias home is a renovation of a good original. That changes the brief in three ways:

  • The layout is an asset, not a problem. Large rooms and clear separation between formal, family and private areas suit how many families live. Most owners need to update the plan, not reinvent it.
  • The hidden systems are the real age. Wiring, plumbing, air-conditioning and waterproofing installed in the 2000s may not suit today's loads and expectations, even when the surfaces look fine.
  • You are working in an occupied, managed building. Society approvals, work hours, lift use and neighbours shape the programme.

What to keep, refresh or replace

ElementUsually keepUsually refreshUsually replace
Room proportions and orientation✔
Marble flooring✔ if soundGrind, polish and repairWhere cracked or patchy
Doors and framesRefinish, new hardwareIf warped or dated in profile
KitchenMost original kitchens
BathroomsFittings, waterproofing, often tiles
Wiring and switchboardsTest and upgradeUndersized circuits, old DBs
Air-conditioningService if efficientOlder systems at end of life
LightingMost original fixtures

A survey before design tells you which column each item falls into. It is the cheapest decision you will make and saves the most money.

Seven design ideas for Aralias apartments

1. Open the kitchen, carefully

Many owners now want the kitchen to connect with the family lounge or dining area. In a tower, some walls are structural and others are not. A structural engineer should confirm which walls can be opened, and the society's approval should be in hand before any wall comes down. Where a full opening is not possible, a wide glazed partition or a pass-through counter gives the same sense of connection. Our kitchen layout guide covers the options.

2. Make the golf-course view the anchor

Arrange the living room, dining table and primary bedroom around the view. Lower, slimmer furniture near the windows keeps sightlines open, and sheer layered curtains with blackouts behind them handle both glare and privacy.

3. Restore the marble before replacing it

Original marble floors can often be ground, repaired and polished to look new. Replacing stone across 5,600 sq ft is costly and disruptive for the whole tower. Restore first, and replace only where the stone has failed.

4. Rebuild bathrooms from the waterproofing up

After fifteen or more years, bathrooms are the area most likely to hide leaks. Strip them to the slab, waterproof, test, then finish. A leak into the apartment below is a much bigger problem in a tower than in a villa.

5. Layer the lighting

Older homes typically rely on ceiling fixtures. Replace them with layers: ambient light, task light in the kitchen and study, accent light on art and joinery, and dimmable scenes for evenings.

6. Add automation without breaking walls

Wireless lighting control, smart switches and app-based air-conditioning control can be added with little chasing of walls. Plan the network, access points and any CCTV or video door phones at the start. See our smart home interior design guide.

7. Bring in contemporary joinery and texture

Replace dated cabinetry with full-height, handle-less wardrobes, veneer or fluted wall panelling and a calmer material palette. For style direction, our comparison of Italian and contemporary luxury interiors helps.

The right order for an Aralias renovation

  1. Survey: structure, services, leaks, floors and the condition of every room.
  2. Brief: how the family lives now and in the next ten years.
  3. Approvals: society rules, work hours and any structural sign-off.
  4. Services: wiring, plumbing, air-conditioning, data and automation.
  5. Wet areas: strip, waterproof and test kitchens and bathrooms.
  6. Floors and ceilings: marble restoration, new ceilings and lighting.
  7. Joinery and finishes: wardrobes, kitchen, panelling, paint.
  8. Furnishing and styling: loose furniture, art, soft furnishings.

Cost and timeline

ItemTypical figure
Luxury interior rate in GurgaonAbout ₹2,500 to ₹8,000+ per sq ft (2026 planning range)
Full-home turnkey with The Omega GroupStarts at ₹15 lakh+, scaling with size and specification
Luxury turnkey timelineTypically 4 to 6 months; renovations with structural or waterproofing work can take longer

What moves the budget most: how much of the services you replace, the kitchen and bathroom specification, whether marble is restored or replaced, imported finishes and automation. For the hidden extras in any renovation, see our guide to hidden interior design costs.

Working in an occupied DLF tower

Aralias is a managed, occupied community. Before you fix a schedule:

  • Ask the estate or society office for the current renovation rules: approvals, refundable deposits, work hours and lift use.
  • Plan noisy work (demolition, grinding) within permitted hours and tell neighbours in advance.
  • Protect common corridors and lifts during material movement.
  • Keep debris removal on a schedule; it is one of the most common causes of friction.

Aralias, Magnolias and Camellias: same corridor, different briefs

The three DLF5 condominiums share Golf Course Road but not the same brief. The Aralias homes are older and mostly renovation projects. The Camellias are newer, larger and usually bare-shell fit-outs — see our DLF Camellias interior design guide. For the corridor-level picture, see what makes Golf Course Road interiors different.

faqs.question: How big are DLF Aralias apartments?
faqs.answer: DLF lists 254 residences across 11 towers. Listings show 4BHK apartments of roughly 5,600 to 6,000 sq ft and penthouses of about 10,000 sq ft and above. Confirm the exact size from your own sale documents.

faqs.question: Can I open the kitchen in a DLF Aralias apartment?
faqs.answer: Often, partly. Some walls in a tower are structural, so a structural engineer must confirm which can be opened, and the society must approve the work. A glazed partition or pass-through counter is a good alternative where a full opening is not possible.

faqs.question: Should I replace the original marble flooring?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. Original marble can usually be ground, repaired and polished. Replace it only where the stone has cracked or failed, since full replacement is expensive and disruptive in an occupied tower.

faqs.question: How long does an Aralias renovation take?
faqs.answer: Luxury turnkey projects in Gurgaon typically take 4 to 6 months. Renovations that replace services, rebuild bathrooms or need structural approval can take longer, so plan back from your move-in date.

faqs.question: What should be checked before renovating an older luxury apartment?
faqs.answer: Check the structure, wiring capacity, plumbing, air-conditioning, waterproofing in wet areas, and the condition of floors and doors. A survey tells you what to keep, refresh or replace before any design work starts.

faqs.question: Do I need society approval for interior work in DLF Aralias?
faqs.answer: Yes, for most significant work. Ask the estate office for current rules on approvals, deposits, work hours and lift use, and get any structural change signed off before demolition begins.
